title: Should I convert my VX Ace project into MZ?

posts.author: Darkbeetlebot
posts.body:
I recently started working on my very old, previously abandoned VXAce project again. Thing is, the engine is very out of date and has some annoying restrictions. Now, I only got MZ recently, so I don't know how much it improved, but my main concern is about how easy it would be to port the old project into the new and if MZ has the scripts that I need and use in my old project.
For my old project, I used pretty much
all
of yanfly's scripts. Core, Battle, Save, Battle Command List, Message System, Status Menu, Move Restrict Region, Skill Restrictions, Victory Aftermath, Adjust Limits, AOE, Base Troop Events, Buff & State Manager, Combat Log Display, Death Common Events, Convert Damage, Element Absorb, Element Reflect, Enemy Death Transformations, Enemy HP Bars, Equip Engine, Equip Dynamic Stats, Extra Drops, Extra Param Formulas, Field State Effects, Instant Cast, Lunatic Damage/Gemini, Menu Engine, Party System, Skill cost manager, Shop Options, Passive States, System Options, Target Manager, Weapon Attack Replace, Anti-fail message, Call Event, Event Chase Player, Debug Extension, Spawn Event, Stop All Movement, and Swap Monsters.
On top of this, I also had other scripts by Hime, Mr. Trivel, and others:
Large Choices by Tsukihime
Skills Replace Skills by Fomar0153
Instance Items by Hime
A patch for the above script and Ace Equip Engine
Item Affixes by Hime
Random Affixes by Selchar
Item Rarity by Hime
Conjure Weapons by Mr. Trivel
AI Checks and Tables by Mr. Trivel
Rare Enemies by Mr. Trivel
New Items in Shop on Sell by Mr. Trivel
Item Info by Mr. Trivel
Event Wait Command by Hime
Shop Manager by Hime
Shop Stock by Hime
Random Event Positions by Hime
Count-up Clock by Hime
Element EX by AdiktuzMiko
Slip Damage EX by AdiktuzMiko
Pre-Skill evals by Selchar
Progressive State by Hime
Attack Element Modifiers by Hime
Multiple Normal Attacks (author unknown but its function is absolutely CRUCIAL, allowing for more than one "normal attack" skill to exist)
Minimum Damage by Dekita
Two custom bugfix scrips to fix enemy targeting on dead actors and junk symbols appearing randomly
Word Wrap by KilloZapit
A custom script to make the text progress slower (I am very disappointed with how VX Ace handles message text formatting and I'd love to have as much control as Deltarune's engine gives over that sort of thing.)
At the point I left it in and the point I've refurbished it to in the present, the work was mostly within the project's database. I have nearly 200 common events programmed, about 200 skills, about 100 items, about 180 weapons, 70 armors, 50 enemies, 70 troops, 150 states, 120 animations (some of which had to be manually made), a few frankensteined tilesets, an utterly GARGANTUAN icon set that I found somewhere, can't remember where, a complete terms section, and a ton of custom audio and visual assets. I had also created a whole set of opening cutscenes and began work on the game's first dungeon, using about 90 variables and switches in the process. There is a LOT of dialogue owing to a high amount of branching and player choices causing a large amount of complexity despite actually resulting in something rather short.
The reason I used VX Ace back then was because I didn't like the aesthetic of MV and VXAce's script game back then was much better. Nowadays, I'm not sure. I still prefer the aethetic VXAce's default assets have, but I can't stand the resolution restriction and some of the quirks of the engine itself, especially with regards to the messages.
So am I better off porting this into MZ? Can I do everything there that I can here? Or should I stay on VXAce and just finish the game as it is? I want to decide that before I go rewriting the entire script and making new content.
I realize also that a lot of the things I listed above may come off as arcane to anyone reading. Yanfly is pretty well known and the names of the scripts are fairly self-explanatory, but if anything needs clarification on what functions I need, please tell me.

RPG Maker MZ is a lot superior than VX Ace.
However, since you've done some work at VX Ace, I'd suggest to finish the VX Ace game.
On an alternate approach, why not spend some time on MZ for a while?
In my case, I continued my project on MV when MZ was released, and
I decided to finish it in MV (I already did), after around 20-30 hours spending time fooling around MZ.

posts.author: ZimXero
posts.body:
Can you give an estimate of hours remaining to complete your game?
Can you estimate how many hours it would take to re-assemble what you've done so far?
Is there a significant feature you want to include that MZ has but VXAce does not?
Have you considered releasing a VXAce Chapter1 or demo, then switch to MZ?
Don't commit to an enormous time investment re-coding your game without answering those questions for yourself first.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Darkbeetlebot said:
On top of this, I also had other scripts by Hime, Mr. Trivel, and others:
Click to expand...
Your list means that it will be very difficult to convert the project from VXA to MZ.
The reason is that VXA and MZ use different programming languages - Ruby-based RGSS3 for VXA as opposed to javascript for MZ.
Which means you'll have to replace each and every script with its MZ-equivalent, and that is not only a lot of work but has an additional problem:
VXA needed direct script access to configure the scripts - you edited the code for settings and had to use script functions to call or change the script operation.
MV and MZ provided a much better and more secure interface - but that also means that many things were handled differently even if a script programmer ported his/her own script into a plugin.
Which basically means you'll have to edit and change every single case where you used script code inside an event.
that is not something easy to do if you used script functions in many events...

posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
Anecdote
: I started a game in VX. When VX Ace came out, I converted it to Ace. When MV came out, I converted it to MV, with some additional improvements (such as 3rd party tiles). It still has not progressed very far. During that time I have finished 2 games with MV and have a project that I have made progress on in MZ. Meanwhile, my original game is stuck.
Conclusion
: Sometimes projects stick, and stay stuck. Getting either MV or MZ (or both) may give you pleasure and enhance your creativity, which would be a good thing but might not make you finish your game.
Good luck whatever you choose.

Better performance, for one. Access to mobile build exporting, much better plugin management, more updated plugins that will only increase in number, javascript being less painful than Ruby, better compatibility with newer OS', higher game resolutions, a generally better UI for development, 3-layer mapping (something I missed from XP), built-in side view battle, more versatile character sprite creator, easy to edit vocab, variable and switch searching, user-defined balloon icons, editing while playtesting, and event testing without having to launch the game.
Those are the major upsides, anyways.

That was part of what I was trying to explain.
While any reasonable function will be available in some plugin, it is extremely unlikely for any script to have a direct equivalent in MZ.
Just an example:
Yanfly's set for MV was much expanded over what he had as a script set for VXA, likely containing many of the functions you needed other scripts for. But Visustella (who was paid to port his suite) reorganised a lot to improve performance - Yanfly's Base Troop Plugin became part of the Visustella Battle Core for example.
On the other hand while Tsukihime ported many of her plugins to MV, she left the community before MZ was released. And I haven't seen an equivalent to the dynamic functions of her Equip Core yet (although I haven't looked deeply into MZ plugins because I haven't used MZ yet).

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Darkbeetlebot said:
So you're saying that if I really wanted to port a project to a newer engine, I should use MV instead of MZ because of the scripts?
Click to expand...
not exactly. I'm pointing out where you use the wrong approach and how much workload a successful conversion would be. And then you could make an educated decision whether to convert or not.
The problem with your approach (and why we can't help much with it) is that you'll never get a one-on-one list of "this script converts to this plugin".
What you would have to do is more like
- what function do I use that script for?
- what plugin provides a similar function under MZ?
- do I already have that plugin or something similar?
- after crosschecking, build the new project engine in MZ
Just one example: most of what yanfly's Ace Battle Engine provides (pictures for actors) has become default in MV and MZ, it doesn't even need that script any more. Instead Yanfly (MV) and Visustella (MZ) focused on action sequence in sideview as well as adding skill process notetags that make a lot of your other old script obsolete.
